description: Console lock: first run asks for owner email+password in the browser, then every page and API needs a signed-in session (change password and sign out from Settings). Docker also ships headless Chromium with a boot-time engine check.
features: First run redirects to a setup screen asking for owner email+password (hash only, never plaintext).
Signed-in sessions via HttpOnly cookie; strangers get login-required instead of the console.
Settings can change the password and sign out for real (previously local-only).
install.py owners keep working — same record format on both paths.
Docker image includes headless Chromium; each start logs a browser-engine OK/FAIL line.
Public-link skip is now explicit in container logs (needs X5_PUBLIC=1 plus a logged-in client).
